The fall mainly reflected applicants bringing filings forward into 2013 ahead of the **Raising the Bar reforms**, which raised the inventive threshold for standard patents. The 2015 report attributed the unusually high 2013 total to early filing of applications that would otherwise have been filed in 2014.[1]

IP Australia received **25,947 standard patent applications in 2014, down 13 per cent from 2013**.[2] The subsequent rebound supports this timing explanation: applications rose 10 per cent in 2015, returning to their normal growth trend.[3]

citations.quote: This law was designed to increase the inventive threshold required for an innovation to be granted as a standard patent.
It can reasonably be assumed that the historically high number of applications in 2013 was caused by the early filing of applications which otherwise would have been filed in 2014.

claims.text: Applications rebounded by 10 per cent in 2015 and returned to their normal growth trend, supporting the timing explanation.
